messages.author: ddc0f9f14283caab
messages.subject: Alignment of indels
parts:
Hi,

I have been trying to test the ability of various sequence aligners to align reads containing indels to genomic DNA. As a test example, I have been using an insertion in an enhancer of the TAL1 gene described in a number of leukemic cell lines (www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/25394790) and I have been using the MOLT3 H3K27ac data from the same paper.

So far I have tested a number of algorithms including BWA, GSNAP and subread. Of the three algorithms, only GSNAP has so far been able to detect a single read containing an 'AC' insertion corresponding to that reported in the paper (see attached IGV screenshot - subread alignment is in the top panel and GSNAP in the bottom panel). A clear visual description of the insertion can be seen in Figure 1 of the above paper (https://d2ufo47lrtsv5s.cloudfront.net/content/sci/346/6215/1373/F1.large.jpg).

I don't actually know exactly how many reads should be mapping to the insertion. However, it is clear that based on the subread parameters I've used (subread-align -T 12 -I 20 -u -t 1 -i hg19 -r $file -o ../bam/$tmp"_H3K27ac_subread.bam") it is currently not picking up at least one read with the indel that was found by GSNAP.

I am wondering if you have any advice regarding parameters that might help subread detect reads with the indel or soft-clipped reads containing the indel? I would prefer to use subread because it is many times faster than GSNAP.

Thank you for your time. Any help would be very much appreciated.

Jason

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: Alignment of indels
parts:
Hi Jason,

Could you try change -I value to 16 in your command? Subread uses a different approach to detect indels when -I value is greater than 16.

Best,
Wei

messages.author: ddc0f9f14283caab
messages.subject: Re: Alignment of indels
parts:
Hi Wei,
Thanks for the suggestion. Unfortunately it still doesn't detect that particular read using -I 16. I have now also tested novoalign and like GSNAP it also detects that single read with the insertion. Would you have other suggestions? Or would it help if I share the fastq file?
Jason

messages.author: ddc0f9f14283caab
messages.subject: Re: Alignment of indels
parts:
Hi Wei
I just realised that I wasn't showing the softclipped reads in IGV. The screenshot above shows that subread (the last two tracks with -I 20 and -I16 simply softclipped the read with the insertion). I guess this means that it just has something with the gap penalties used?
Jason

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: Alignment of indels
parts:
Hi Jason,

Thanks for providing further information. To detect an indel, Subread needs to have at least one read that contains perfected matched 16bp mers at both sides of the indel. For the insertion you are interested in, the number bases at its left side in each read are too short (<16bp) and therefore Subread cannot detect them.

If you can increase your sequencing depth (eg. by merging together the replicates if you have), Subread might be able to detect it if Subread can find a read which includes matched 16 mers flanking the indel from both sides.

The reason why Subread requires the presence of 16bp mers flanking each indel is to ensure a high accuracy for its indel calling.

Best,
Wei
